title: Тренировка для папы  (Practice for a Dad)

segments.t: Seconds after Kostya leaves, 'calm' little Styopa breaks a dish in the apartment, and an urgent phone call from German forces Vika to rush to the restaurant and leave Max in charge.
А что мне с ним делать?
Тренируйся, представь, что это наш сын.
Let's examine each line as Vika hands babysitting duty over to Max.
'Calm, you say?' Max wonders warmly in the scene, putting "spokoynyy" ("calm") alongside "govorish" ("you say") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'What did you break?' Vika tests quietly to keep things clear, anchoring the Russian line on "razbil" ("wrecked, crashed") and "ty" ("you") without extra filler.
'That was not me, that was Styopa.' Max keeps an emphatic attitude at once, weaving "styopka" ("styopa") together with "eto" ("this") just the way native speakers do.
'Kostya asked us to look after him.' Max presents a frank mood across the room, putting "poprosil" ("asked") alongside "prismotret" ("to look") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'He is a cool kid, right?' Max prompts sharply to German here, building the phrase around "klassnyy" ("great") and "malysh" ("kid, little one") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'He is a cute boy.' Vika brings a frank rhythm as they talk, combining "simpatichnyy" ("handsome, cute") and "malchik" ("boy") so the key meaning lands right away.
'I still need to unpack my things.' Vika maintains an emphatic tone with German, joining "yeshchyo" ("more, still") to "nado" ("it is necessary") so every word pulls its weight.

'Viktoriya, come to the restaurant urgently.' German offers an easygoing attitude in front of Vika, leaning on "srochno" ("urgent, urgently") before closing the thought with "priyezzhayte" ("to come, to arrive").
'We have been robbed!' German sustains a warm stance in the scene, putting "obokrali" ("to robbed") alongside "nas" ("us") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Yes, I will be right there.' Vika sustains a lively manner on the spot, linking "seychas" ("now"), "budu" ("will be"), and "da" ("yes") in one brisk exchange.
'Styopa is staying with you.' Vika establishes a warm tempo across the room, putting "styopa" ("styopa") alongside "ostayotsya" ("stays") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
А что мне с ним делать?
'And what am I supposed to do with him?' Max tests honestly right away, building the phrase around "delat" ("do") and "chto" ("what") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Тренируйся, представь, что это наш сын.
'Practice, imagine that he is our son.' Vika brings a natural position across the room, anchoring the Russian line on "treniruysya" ("practice") and "predstav" ("imagine") without extra filler.
'He is climbing into the oven right now!' Max brings a resolute course for Vika, putting "seychas" ("now") alongside "lezet" ("goes in, fits") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
А что мне с ним делать?
Тренируйся, представь, что это наш сын.
Remember that false friend in Vika's reply — the word that sounds like 'sympathetic' actually means 'cute' or 'pleasant-looking' in Russian. See you next time!
